title: Hybrid retrieval: fixed benchmark excerpt
body: Dense vector retrieval matches semantic meaning. Sparse keyword retrieval, such as BM25, matches lexical terms. Hybrid retrieval runs vector and keyword search and merges ranked results, for example using reciprocal rank fusion. Keyword matches help when identifiers or rare terms are poorly represented by embeddings. Running both paths adds indexing and query complexity; latency depends on the implementation. A benchmark engineering inference is to prefer hybrid retrieval when both semantic paraphrases and exact terms matter, while checking failures and ranking quality on representative queries. This fixed fixture is not live web evidence.
